## Three Coins Fellowship

The Three Coins Fellowship were a small adventuring company active in the Delimbiyr Vale in the late 14 century DR. They comprised Kars, a human ranger; Douver, half-elf bard; and Eman, a dwarf warrior.

History
Only newly formed in the summer of the, the Three Coins Fellowship visited the city of Loudwater in early Eleasis. They had heard the story of a ghost that wandered Tragedy's Grotto after each Shieldmeet and of how those who followed it were said to find great treasure, or else sorrow and doom. They, of course, wanted the treasure, and were driven largely by this greed. Strangely, they'd heard this story from a feminine voice in their heads, one calling itself Tymora, the goddess of luck, and promising enough riches to become kings. They had little plan beyond that.

In the streets of Loudwater late one night, the trio encountered the ghost for themselves, finding it to be the spirit of a robed monk. It ignored them, and when Eman leapt to grab it, he fell through and into the muddy road. Thus, they followed it to Tragedy's Grotto and the hoped-for treasure. When another band of adventurers came across them, the trio had no desire to share and would refuse conversation and assistance with increasing vehemence, from Douver politely asking them to mind their own business to Kars spitting threats and foul language and warning shots from his bow.

One way or another, the Three Coins Fellowship and the other adventurers followed the ghost to Tragedy's Grotto. There, it sunk into the ground and the buried vault there. Then both groups were ambushed by groundlings in Zhentarim employ, with Kars, Eman, and Douver being targeted as they were first to arrive.

If they survived the battle, Eman, Douver, and/or Kars joined the other adventurers in exploring a buried vault the ghost had entered, finding no treasure but the mysterious shard of the Fallen One. However, one of the three would become crazed, being possessed by a magical force of lawful and evil nature and attacked the others to seize the shard, whatever the cost. If subdued and questioned, he would be confused and have no memory of it. They might be persuaded to speak of the voice they'd heard, but if forcefully interrogated or magically compelled to explain why he'd attacked the others, he would be possessed again, screeching fiendishly the cryptic words "Because the key is mine!" He would then be choked to death from the unseen force; only a protection from evil or protection from law spell could prevent it. Should he be rescued, he would reveal a cruel and evil presence had been in his mind. The other adventurers took the shard and followed the trail of its mystery to the Phantoms' Cloister.The identity of this apparent possessing force is unknown—the module says this will be explained in the second part, Secret of Phantoms' Cloister, but this was never published. Being lawful evil and "fiendish", it may be a devil.

## The Nathlum

The Nathlum was an infamous book of spells and poison recipes compiled sometime in or before the 10 century DR.

Description
The book had a gray canvas cover into which was sewn curling brown parchment pages. Although nondescript in appearance, the book was protected by immensely powerful and evil magic. Any good person who held The Nathlum suffered constant burning pain in their head and blinding pain in their eyes, which was intense enough to kill them if they did not relinquish the book. This magic was resistant to any normal attempt to dispel it.

Contents

The Nathlum detailed recipes for sixteen potent poisons, most notably belpren, dwarfbane, huld, jeteye, lhurdas, orvas, prespra, ulcrun, and varrakas.

It also contained four unique glyphs of warding, each of which could only be cast by an evil cleric and could only harm those who were good. These glyphs were known as curtal, hlack, yammas, and zuth.

The tome was also known to contain the formula for the maze spell.

History
Both the meaning of the name and the true origins of The Nathlum were unknown.

The first presumed record of The Nathlum was made by the sage Orfidel, who described a tome matching its description in the possession of the evil mage Lethchauntos sometime prior to the Orcfastings War of the . At the time, Lethchauntos dwelt among orcish followers of Wund, a shaman of Yurtrus in Uruth Ukrypt.

During the Orcfastings War, the book was claimed by Tymor Threeshields as part of his spoils, and the first official record of the tome's existence appeared in his accountings. It was believed that he was eager to rid himself of the book, and subsequently sent The Nathlum to Neverwinter as part of a dowry for his daughter, Nulauznee. The book then vanished from records.

It was not until the mid–14 century DR that The Nathlum reappeared, still seemingly complete, when it came into the possession of the wizard Phrandjas in Port Llast. Despite the great pain that reading the tome inflicted upon him, Phrandjas persevered in reading and making notes about the book, which he shared with the likes of Elminster (who would go on to disseminate knowledge about how to recognize some of the poisons and glyphs). Phrandjas also copied the recipes for the tome's various poisons with the intention of selling them to local alchemists, although it was unclear if he had shared them as of the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

## Tharos imposter

A Tharos imposter was a traitorous member of the Fraternity of Tharos who sought to undermine their evil schemes.

Activities
Such an imposter may have joined the Fraternity with the goal to infiltrate it or may have turned against the faction in hopes of atoning for the evil that the initiation rites forced them to commit. Either way, imposters tended to be driven by hatred and fury directed at their demon-worshiping fellows. Even so, they operated with subtlety, relying on their knowledge, guile, and lies to stop the Fraternity's plots and chip away at their power while maintaining the appearance of a loyal cultist. They were known to feed information to and even to join adventuring groups fighting against the Fraternity.

Prerequisites
Imposters were natives of Impiltur who despised what the Fraternity was doing to the people of their land. To successfully oppose the Fraternity required both the arcane abilities of a warlock and the guile of a rogue.

Abilities
In battle, imposters harnessed their great fury at the Fraternity as well as their great talent for lies and misdirection. They were also able to wield the spells and demonic magic associated with the cult, calling upon hellfire, demons, and burning ash to slay their foes.

## Thay infiltrator

Thay infiltrators were a small group of Aglarondan loyalists who utilized both stealth and divine magic to become expert spies and scouts within the borders of Thay during the late 15 century DR.

Activities
Only a few Thay infiltrators existed, and were known for their bravery, speed, and efficiency. Their experience behind enemy lines made them experts at navigating Thay as well as natural leaders for any expedition onto Thayan soil.

A Thay infiltrator used their skills, magic, and knowledge to conduct reconnaissance for Aglarond's military as well as to complete dangerous missions into Thayan territory, such as to retrieve an important object, rescue an abductee, or serve as a guide for a team with a specific objective to complete.

Prerequisites
Becoming a Thay infiltrator required the skills of a ranger and also those of a cleric, or at least the ability to channel holy power to use spells such as healing word. Only those who lived in and were loyal to Aglarond would become Thay infiltrators.

Abilities
The blending of holy power with subterfuge was the hallmark of a Thay infiltrator. Their sacred stealth allowed them to quickly maneuver and hide away from foes, and they could call upon a veil of glittering divine lights to conceal themselves and their allies from sight. They favored ranged weapons and would energize their projectiles with radiant energy, which they could use to blind their enemies. More experienced infiltrators mastered the skills of simultaneously healing their allies while firing upon their enemies, and in some cases, firing a barrage of divinely charged projectiles all at once.

## The Ancestor

The Ancestor was the appellation of a very old drow male who led the Ancient Ones, a group of Maztican drow, in the 14th century DR.

Description

He normally kept his face hidden under a dark hood and wore dark cloth. He had a narrow head with thin white hair that revealed his black scalp. His limbs seemed like they were only bone and his figure was skeletal.

He was proficient in Hishna magic and wielded a staff that had a tip that resembled the outspread claws of a dragon. This wand produced tiny rays of light that merged into a bolt that struck its target with great force

History

Establishment of the Ancient Ones
In the 10th century DR, the Rockfire cataclysm took place that destroyed much of the underdark beneath the Trackless Sea and Maztica. The Ancestor's tribe were able to escape the destruction and came to the surface in Maztica.

The Ancestor blamed Lolth for abandoning them in the Rockfire. His tribe abandoned their worship of Lolth and embraced Zaltec, the Maztican god of war, who they turned to for their survival in this new world. They came to settle in the Highcave in Mount Zatal neighbouring Nexal and promoted the cult of Zaltec among the native humans, presenting themselves as supernatural beings sent by Zaltec, while keeping their true natures a secret from them. They thus became the Ancient Ones, with the Ancestor serving as their leader.

Within Mount Zatal, the Ancestor kept the Darkfyre, a powerful magical focus into which the hearts of victims sacrificed to Zaltec were fed in order to increase its power. The Ancestor harnessed the power of the Darkfyre for advancing the cult of Zaltec, and thus increasing the power of the Ancients Ones who led the cult as well as his own power as their leader. Through the Darkfyre, Zaltec granted powerful abilities to the Ancestor, including the ability to see events decades in the future and to be given knowledge about what actions needed to be taken to achieve the vision of the future where he would triumph.

Preparation for the coming of the Golden Legion

Sometime in the 14th century DR, he was given a vision where he saw a possible future that could be achieved wherein the cult of Zaltec would reign supreme over Maztica. In order to achieve this, he saw that a group of mercenaries from Faerûn needed to come to Nexal and take Naltecona, the ruler of Nexal as their captive. When Naltecona was killed in their custody, all of Nexal would rise united in great anger against the foreigners under the leadership of the Viperhands, who were zealots of Zaltec under the control of the Ancient Ones. This would then usher in a new age where Nexal and eventually all of Maztica would fall under the complete dominance of the cult of Zaltec.

But the Ancestor also saw in his visions that Zaltec's brother, the god Qotal, had planted a variable that could spell disaster to these plans. This variable was Qotal's chosen priestess Erixitl of Palul, and the only way for their plans to succeed would be if she died before Naltecona was killed.

The Ancestor sent his daughter Darien to Faerûn sometime around ca. 1350 DR. As an albino drow, she was able to present herself as an elf to the unsuspecting people of Faerûn. According to her father's plan, she found Cordell, the leader of a mercenary company after a defeat in a battle. She assisted him and she joined the ranks of his mercenaries to become the mage of the Golden Legion. She remained with them for 10 years, before they embarked to sail westwards from Amn to find a new route to Kara-Tur in 1361 DR, but instead arrived in the previously unknown continent of Maztica.

Also around 1350 DR, the Ancestor had identified Erixitl of Palul, who was only a child at the time, and the Ancient Ones made arrangements to have her killed, lest she thwart the prophesy when she later became an adult. However, through the intervention of a Couatl servant of Qotal, she was captured by Kultakan slavers and taken to Kultaka, where she remained there for many years hidden from the Ancient Ones and from the Ancestor.

Closer to the time when the Legion was to arrive in Maztica, the Ancient Ones discovered that Erixitl was alive in Kultaka and tried to kill her again, but again, through Qotal's intervention, she was sold by her master to another master who took her to Ulatos. The Ancient Ones again tried to have her killed in Ulatos. The Ancestor, fearing that the humans would fail, sent Spirali, one of the Ancient Ones to go himself and find Erixitl to kill her. Spirali, however, also failed and was slain in the attempt.
Coming of the Legion

The Ancestor was surprised by how quickly the Golden Legion were able to defeat the Payit of Ulatos, but had confidence that things would go differently when they would later fight in Nexal. Although there was a risk that when Spirali was killed, the men of Faerûn might have realized that he was a drow and then exposed their secret to the people of Maztica, the Ancestor didn't care as the events had already progressed to a point where this detail would become insignificant.

Erixitl came to Nexal with Halloran a deserter from the Legion who had protected her by killing Spirali. They were welcomed by Naltecona into his palace, and the Ancestor ordered for them both to be killed. Several assassins were sent, but they also failed.

The Ancestor, increasing impatient and enraged by the failures, as the day when Naltecona should die was becoming increasingly closer, threatened Hoxitl, high priest of Zaltec in Nexal, whom had been tasked with killing her for the previous 10 years since she was first identified, that he would die himself if she continued to lived.  He sent the Ancient Ones themselves to search Nexal for her in addition to alerting the priests of Zaltec to locate and destroy her.

Naltecona was killed by Darien according to the plan on the Night of Wailing, but Erixitl still lived. Darien, came to her father to bring him news of the failure. Although his visions had told him that she needed to die before Naltecona's death, the Ancestor reasoned that maybe there was still hope and that if they killed her quickly, then whatever she was going to do to stop them would not occur. Darien informed her father that she believed Erixitl would come to the Highcave by her own free will in order to confront them and he then made plans for her arrival.

Erixitl and her brother Shatil, Halloran and Chitikas, the couatl who had protected Erixitl, arrived at the Highcave to confront the Ancient Ones. The Ancient One used his staff against Erixitl, which was powerful enough to overcome the powerful Pluma protections that she wore. As he was about to kill her, Chitikas plunged into the Ancestor and fought him next to the Darkfyre caldron. During their melee, Chitikas plunged both himself and the Ancestor into the caldron.

The Darkfyre then caused Mount Zatal to explode and Nexal was destroyed. Lolth succeeded in corrupting the Darkfyre to cause the explosion to transform the surviving Ancient Ones into driders. The Ancestor's plans for their domination of Maztica had all come to ruin.

## The Familiar 1/Den of Chaos

Den of Chaos is a short story by Amber Scott for Baldur's Gate: Siege of Dragonspear. The story was published in The Familiar 1.

Summary
Some time in the 1360s DR, Schael Corwin, a member of the Flaming Fist mercenary company, is on a temporary assignment in the Wood of Sharp Teeth with her new partner, a cheerful but clumsy half-elf wizard named Zeri. Their mission is to recover stolen alchemical mushroom samples, belonging to the noblewoman Lady Teritha.

Corwin's tracking leads them to a bandit camp. As they prepare to attack, Corwin recognizes the bandits as her former associates from before she joined the Flaming Fist, led by a man named Derrion.

Despite her history with them, Corwin attempts an arrest. The situation erupts into a fight. During the battle, one bandit, Liina, smashes a box containing the volatile alchemical ingredients to spite Corwin. The mingling gases transform Derrion into a horrific, melting slime that attacks everyone. Corwin, Zeri, and a terrified Liina are forced to work together to destroy the monster with sword and fire.

In the aftermath, a shaken Corwin accepts Liina's surrender. They salvage what remains of the cargo and begin the trek back to the Flaming Fist fortification with their prisoner. The story ends with a quiet moment underscoring the mission's cost and Corwin's growth into a more nuanced individual capable of mercy and understanding the complexities of the wilds.

## The Black Sam Tavern

The Black Sam tavern was a gambling den in the city of Liara within the Domains of Dread.

Structure
It was a rather large building.

Interior
The ground floor was a kitchen and tavern, with numerous booths for privacy. The first floor was a gambling den, and the last floor was Sam's residence.

Atmosphere
The ground floor had a fire pit at the center; the second floor was smoky and poorly lit.

Services
Besides the drinks, there was gambling. Interestingly, the tavern remained open at night, unlike most of Liara's establishments.

Defenses
Sam employed four enforcers, all of them experienced fighters.

History
Though the merchants had fought hard to keep gamblers out of their quarter in Liara, they had met with only limited success. They were able to nip all gambling dens in the bud, but Sam the Nimble somehow managed to establish his own.

At some point in the mid-to-late 14 century DR, adventurers from Ravens Bluff were drawn into the Mists, and came to Liara in Nova Vaasa, where a werespider had been killing people. They were almost certainly impressed into helping discover the killer, suspected to be a vampire; the first victim once they'd accepted might happen while they were at the Black Sam tavern.

## The Boar's Tusk (Ravenloft)

The Boar's Tusk was a tavern in the city of Liara in Nova Vaasa, one of the Domains of Dread.

Location
It was in the Merchant's Quarter of Liara.

Structure
It was a two-story structure, with the inn registry and an adjoining tavern on the first floor and twenty guest rooms on the upper story.

Interior
Each guest room had a comfortable bed, a work table, a wash basin, and a bathtub.

Services
The Boar's tusk had drinks and beds.

History
In the mid-to-late 14 century DR, adventurers from Ravens Bluff somehow came to the Domains of Dread, finding their way to Liara at some point. There, the directions they asked for got them to the Boar's Tusk in the Merchant's Quarter, where they were most likely hired by Turkin Varringore to catch a suspected vampire who had killed six people so far. Among the payment they were offered, there were five nights at the tavern/inn itself.

## The Twelve

The Twelve was an arcane order of wizards, artificers, and sages in the world of Eberron. They were devoted to researching and applying magic both modern and ancient.

History
During the mid-1480s DR of Faerûn, the fiendish Lords of Dust conspired to break into the Spinner's Prison and managed to partially free the Spinner of Shadows. This led to Lolth herself forming the Rift Between Worlds, connecting the prison to the Demonweb Pits and allowing the Spinner to escape. Worse, the rift continued to expand and threatened to eventually destroy Eberron as well.

The Twelve joined the Church of the Silver Flame and the Gatekeepers in trying to study and contain the portal, though they could make little sense of the situation. The Gatekeeper Tavnar Kronnak then decided to send a team of heroes through the rift and hopefully find a solution. The heroes ended up meeting Elminster, found their way to Eveningstar, and fought against Lolth as she attempted to conquer the the Weave.

## The Oni's Right Hand

Oni no Migite or The Oni's Right Hand is a Japanese-language adventure module released on July 28, 2025, on the Dungeons & Dragons Japan website for use in learn-to-play games in Japan, beginning in August. It was written by Masaki Yanagida, who also created pre-generated characters, and features character illustrations by Toshiaki Takayama. Intended as a starting adventure for Dragon of Icespire Peak from the Dungeons & Dragons Essentials Kit, it takes place in the Phandalin region and involves adventurers from Wa and Kozakura searching for an artifact named the Glove of Oni Claw.

## The Narwhal

The Narwhal was a tavern in the Central Port of Skullport in the late 14 century DR.

Structure
The Narwhal was a one-story building in poor condition.

Interior
The tavern's only notable feature was a horn mounted above the mantelpiece. The owner claimed that the horn originated from a sea creature of the Shining Sea, though in truth it was the horn of a unicorn.

Services
Regarded by locals as a seedy dive, the cheap ale served was diluted, the food was of low quality and often infested with insects, and service was largely absent under the inattentive and frequently drunken management of its proprietor.

Inhabitants
Circa 1370 DR, the owner of the Narwhal was Hugo Littlestaff. He purchased day-old mushroom bread from Orthon Calliar, owner of the Tumbling Bugbear.

## Thanbard Krys

Thanbard Krys was a hunter who operated out of Eveningstar in the 15 century DR.

Description
Thanbard was a ruddy human man with light brown hair and a pointed beard.

History

Following the Sschindylryn invasion of Eveningstar and Shadovar invasion of Wheloon, Thanbard was out hunting in the Storm Horns with Olyce Tidewater when they were ambushed by orcs serving Archwizard Amskar. The pair escaped back to Eveningstar, though Thanbard's leg was injured in the process. They noticed the odd behaviour of the orcs, which coincided with the failed raid upon Eveningstar that the Purple Dragons defeated. They ended up on the Eveningstar bridge, bandaging up Thanbard's wound while the Harpers Kara Patwin and Lorant Tass organized a full investigation into the strange events.

## The Sultry Siren

The Sultry Siren was a festhall in the city of Calimport, Calimshan, in the late 14 century DR. It was fully controlled by the Jhasinnar Sodality guild.

Location
It was located on the eastern edge of Gagi Drudach, Axash Sabban, in the city's Emerald Ward.

Activities
A lavish building, it offered services by the female concubines known as jhasinnar. It was well known to be controlled by the Jhasinnar Sodality so most customers were only interested in its pleasures. However, this was a cover: guild leader Ralahn el Matyr used it for trading goods on the black market and fencing stolen jewelry.

Interior
From the cellars, secret passages connected to the Muzad, the undercity of Calimport. These allowed pashas and sultans a discreet escape from their enemies, or just embarrassment, so they owed Ralahn and the Sodality a favor for their lives or their reputations.

History
In the, the Trades Conflagration blazed across northern and central Calimport. The Sultry Siren was damaged, but calling in some favors, Ralahn had it repaired in less than a month.

## Tharmalos

Tharmalos was a great green dragon that dwelled in Cormyr during the mid-1480s DR.

History

During the Sschindylryn invasion of Eveningstar, Tharmalos was hired by the drow to poison the groundwater of Eveningstar. The dragon was joined by a contingent of yuan-ti who helped secure the underground caverns, but when the toxic water was noticed Unmar Halberg allowed a team of adventurers to explore the well. They quickly found the yuan-ti and fought their way through Fless-onas, Gresl-glis, and Saz-sass, before encountering the unexpected dragon. Tharmalos initially thought they were simply a meal delivery, and only realized the error too late before being slain.
